units.translation: Sylburgius wrongly introduced the genitive ἀρούρων [of the fields] into the corrupt fragment 15 (in Etym. M. p. 341, 5) in place of ἀρόρων, which is more similar to the genitive αρότρων [of the plows] corrupted from ἀρότων [of the plowings]. See ἐνηλύσια.

The field of ruin harvests death.

A word not known elsewhere, noted by Hesychius: ἀρρυσίαστον [not to be dragged away]: ἄσυλον [inviolable], ἀνενεχυρίαστον [not subject to seizure] (thus Schmidt for ἀνε . . χυρίαστον). Here it means nothing more than not dragged away, not claimed as slaves, as the use of the verb ῥυσιάζεσθαι [to be dragged away] teaches at v. 424: μηδ᾽ ἴδης με ἐξ ἑδρᾶν πολυθέων ῥυσιασθεῖσαν [do not see me dragged from the seats of the many gods].
That we dwell in this land as free and not subject to seizure (written with a single p in M) and with inviolability from mortals.
